title: TAT-3312 — Size slider at 100% must not show Insufficient funds
description: Navigates to the ETH perps order-entry screen with a funded account, sets size to 100% via the percentage input, and proves the submit button shows the normal trade action label (Open long ETH) instead of a false 'Insufficient funds' error. Reverting the fix (amount rounds up past available margin) makes ac1-assert-submit-actionable time out.

notes: Active account is the funded testnet perps account; do not switch accounts.

Balance and price stream live from HyperLiquid and DRIFT between runs — the recipe must not hardcode any amount; it gates on stable labels + a non-zero-balance signal and asserts the margin relationship.
Default leverage 3 -> maxSize = availableBalance * 3; the fix floors the 100% amount to 2dp so margin (amount/leverage) <= availableBalance and the submit button stays actionable.

setup-status.detail: Confirm the extension adapter is connected before driving the UI.

setup-navigate-order-entry.intent: Open the ETH perps order-entry screen
setup-navigate-order-entry.detail: Raw extension hash route /perps/trade/:symbol for the order form.

ac1-screenshot-submit-actionable.note: AC1: size at 100% — submit button reads 'Open long ETH', no Insufficient funds error.
ac1-screenshot-submit-actionable.intent: Capture visual proof of the actionable submit button at 100% size
ac1-screenshot-submit-actionable.detail: Visual evidence for AC1 (mixed proof mode).

teardown-end.detail: AC1 proven: 100% size shows the normal trade action label.

ac1-drive-max-size.intent: Drive the size to 100% (React-correct native setter) and verify the submit button is actionable
ac1-drive-max-size.detail: The harness ui.set_input assigns el.value directly, which React's value-tracker swallows so onChange never fires and the amount never recomputes. This driver uses the native value-setter (the real user keystroke) so handlePercentInputChange fires; it waits for the live (drifting) balance to load, drives 100%, then asserts the submit button reads 'Open long ETH' and that 'Insufficient funds' is absent — proving margin (amount/leverage) <= availableBalance after the floor fix. Exits non-zero if the bug is present. No balance/amount is hardcoded.

ac1-assert-actionable.intent: AC1: fix verified — 100% size is actionable, not 'Insufficient funds'
ac1-assert-actionable.detail: Driver exit 0 means the submit button was actionable at 100% size with no insufficient-funds error.
